issues.title: Please Make a burst mode optional.
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**


Sometimes Telegram Account Limited Error occurs. As you know, telegram Account Limited Error is an error which happens when an account sends many messages at once. This does not cause any permanent issues with the account. But When this error happens tgcf will not send any more messages via the account. (Temporary wait limit)


**Describe the solution you'd like**


It would be very helpful if you provided message rate options. 

example : [burst mode - High or Low]

It will be able to reduce the frequency of occurrence of the telegram Account Limited Error.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**


Alternatively, it would be fine to be able to set the interval between sending messages in seconds. 

example: sent every [10] seconds




Thank you! This project is evolving every day.

issues.title: Clash of identical visible names of chat
issues.body:
Hello and thank you for your work. I've been using your script and is working really good. But i encountered a problem. Telegram allows identical names for chats visible names, only their user-names are unique. So i wanted to copy files from 3 public channels to my private channel, but these public channels names are the same. So the script only copied files from one of this channels. 

How does your script differentiate between channels that have identical visible names? There must be a way to separate them and uniquely identify them. Is there a possibility to use user-names of channels instead of visible names?

issues.title: Grouped Media Sent as Individual Messages – Album Support Missing
issues.body:
Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Yes. When forwarding messages automatically, TGCF breaks up grouped messages (such as media albums) that were originally sent together as one unit in the source channel. Instead of forwarding them as a grouped album, TGCF sends each item individually, which disrupts the original format and user experience.

Describe the solution you'd like
I would like TGCF to preserve message grouping (albums) when forwarding from one channel to another. If the original messages are part of a media group (e.g., a photo album), TGCF should forward them together in the same grouped format instead of sending them one by one.

Describe alternatives you've considered
I considered manually forwarding the messages to preserve the grouping, but this defeats the purpose of automation. Another option might be writing a custom script using Telethon or Pyrogram, but it would be much more efficient if TGCF handled this natively.

issues.title: Plugin to prevent forwarding of recent duplicate messages
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Sometimes the same TG users post the same info to a different telegram channels in a short time, one after another.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Simple plugin to check last (5) messages we received. Drop any new message that is already in the list. Forward message otherwise, and add it to the list. Drop one element from list if it contains more than (5) element.

Later we can expand on the simple implementation to solve problems like this: https://github.com/aahnik/tgcf/issues/57

issues.body:
### Describe the bug


### Description

`tdl login -f` works normally and can successfully recognize/login to the account.

However, after login, `tdl chat ls` and other commands that require a Telegram connection fail.

The connection appears to be established initially, but the MTProto messages from Telegram are rejected with:

```text
bad message id 7684180989355890689:
created too far in future: message rejected
```

The same error continues on every retry.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run:

```bash
tdl login -f
```

The login process completes successfully.

2. Then run:

```bash
tdl chat ls
```

3. The command fails after approximately 25 seconds.

Other `tdl` commands that require a Telegram connection show the same behavior.

### Relevant logs

The log shows that the connection is restored and then switches to DC 5:

```text
Connection restored from state
Initialized {"v": "v0.140.0", "conn_id": 0, "dc_id": 5}
```

The connection then receives a rejected message:

```text
bad message id 7684180989355890689:
created too far in future: message rejected
```

The client retries the request multiple times, but every attempt encounters the same problem. Eventually:

```text
Retry limit reached
```

and:

```text
initConnection: invoke: rpcDoRequest: retryUntilAck:
retry limit reached after 5 attempts
```

The connection is then restarted and the same problem occurs again.


### Additional information

The important point is that **`tdl login -f` itself works correctly**, while subsequent commands fail when initializing the MTProto connection.

See the attached full debug log.

issues.title: [Bug] `tdl dl` crashes with "fatal error: concurrent map iteration and map write" in saveProgress when download is interrupted
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When a download fails mid-run (e.g. network drop), `tdl dl` frequently dies with a Go runtime fatal error instead of a graceful error:

```
fatal error: concurrent map iteration and map write

goroutine 22 [running]:
...
encoding/json.Marshal({0x19a2ee0, 0xc00061a3c0})
        encoding/json/encode.go:209 +0xbe
github.com/iyear/tdl/app/dl.saveProgress({0x20b2c38, 0xc00043a180}, {0x20b1298, 0xc000122900}, 0xc00012d340)
        github.com/iyear/tdl/app/dl/dl.go:209 +0x159
github.com/iyear/tdl/app/dl.Run.func1()
        github.com/iyear/tdl/app/dl/dl.go:94 +0x3a
```

## Root cause

`iter.Finished()` takes the mutex but returns **the live map itself**, not a copy
(`app/dl/iter.go`):

```go
func (i *iter) Finished() map[int]struct{} {
	i.mu.Lock()
	defer i.mu.Unlock()

	return i.finished
}
```

`saveProgress()` then iterates that map via `json.Marshal` **outside the lock**
(`app/dl/dl.go:204-212`), while downloader goroutines are still calling
`iter.Finish(id)` (which writes to the same map under the mutex). Since the
deferred save-progress path runs exactly when the errgroup is being torn down
on error, in-flight goroutines racing with the marshal are common -> the Go
runtime kills the process. As a side effect the resume progress for that run
is not persisted.

### To Reproduce

The race fires whenever the download run is torn down while workers are still
in flight - a network drop and a plain Ctrl+C go through the same code path
(`signal.NotifyContext` -> ctx cancel -> errgroup unwinds -> deferred
`saveProgress` runs concurrently with the last `iter.Finish` calls).

Minimal setup:

1. Export any chat with a few hundred media files:
   ```
   tdl chat export -c <chat> -o e.json
   ```
2. Start the download with default concurrency (`-l 2`, `-t 4` - eno

issues.title: [Bug] Extreme speed throttling (<300 KBps) and downloads failing to start (0 B/s)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

I am experiencing two critical issues while using tdl on Fedora:
Speed Ceiling: Download speeds are consistently throttled and never cross the 300 KBps mark (usually hovering around 160-180 KBps), regardless of thread count or concurrency settings.
Stalled Downloads: Some files in the queue fail to start entirely. They remain at 0.0% [ ... ] [0 B in ...; 0 B/s] indefinitely, while other files in the same session may be progressing (albeit slowly).

### To Reproduce

I have tried various combinations of flags to bypass the throttle, including the following:

tdl dl -f "path/to/output.json" -d "path/to/dir/" --takeout --continue --desc -t 16 -l 1

Even with -l 1 and increased threads, the speed remains under 300 KBps.

### Expected behavior

Speed should reflect available bandwidth (or at least the standard Telegram API limit for non-premium accounts, which is typically higher than 180 KBps).
All files in the queue should eventually initiate the handshake and begin downloading rather than stalling at 0 B/s.

issues.title: Download progress bar scrolls uncontrollably when filenames contain CJK characters
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

```markdown
## Environment
- tdl version: 0.20.4 (commit 9d7d49e)
- OS: Windows 11
- Terminal: Windows Terminal and legacy conhost (reproduced on both)

## Problem
When downloading media whose filenames contain CJK characters (e.g. Chinese),
the progress display scrolls the terminal instead of staying in place. Every
refresh pushes the whole block down by one or more lines, eventually wiping
previous output. Pure-ASCII filenames do not trigger it.

Manually widening the terminal window stops the scrolling, which points to a
line-width calculation issue.

## Steps to reproduce
1. `tdl dl -f <export.json> -d <dir>` against a chat whose media names contain
   Chinese characters.
2. Keep the terminal at its default width (~80 columns).
3. Watch the progress block: it scrolls continuously.

## Root cause
The per-tracker progress line is rendered wider than the terminal because
`github.com/jedib0t/go-pretty/v6` (v6.5.0) truncates the tracker message by
**rune count** instead of **display width**.

Flow:
- tdl's `pkg/prog/prog.go` calls `SetMessageWidth(width * 3 / 5)`.
- go-pretty's `progress.renderTracker` shortens long messages via `text.Snip(...)`.
- `text.Snip` measures width correctly with `RuneWidthWithoutEscSequences`,
  but then delegates the actual cutting to `text.Trim`.
- `text.Trim` increments a counter by one per rune:

```go
func Trim(str string, maxLen int) string {
    // ...
    if outLen < maxLen {
        outLen++          // counts runes, not columns
        out.WriteRune(sChr)
        continue
    }
    // ...
}
```

A CJK character occupies 2 terminal columns, so a message "truncated" to
`maxLen` runes ends up up to ~2× `maxLen` columns wide. The rendered line then
exceeds the terminal width, soft-wraps onto a second row, and
`progr

# Telegram_Backup
Copyright 2016 Fabian Schlenz  
Licensed under GPLv3

## State of this project
The tool is working, but not really as intended: Media files in most cases can't be downloaded, message downloads are hit with 30 second delays after every 200 messages. Some users reported getting banned by Telegram without reason after using this tool (with many users not getting banned at the same time, so this could theoretically just be a coincidence).

### Where do you save the files?
The files are being saved in your User directory in a folder named
`telegram_backup`. Under windows, this would typically be under
`C:\Users\<username>\telegram_backup`. Linux users should look unter
`/home/<username>/.telegram_backup`.

Also for people who want to create a backup of a huge account using telegram_backup a feature to import a .json File of all messages created by the Telegram Desktop data export tool would already be super helpful.

readme_amostras.texto:
# Installation

You need Python3 (3.6 works fine, 3.5 will crash randomly).

Install dependencies by running this command:

|--------------------------|:-----------------------:|--------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------|
| `TELEGRAM_DAEMON_API_ID`   | `--api-id`              | api_id from https://core.telegram.org/api/obtaining_api_id   |                     |
| `TELEGRAM_DAEMON_API_HASH` | `--api-hash`            | api_hash from https://core.telegram.org/api/obtaining_api_id |                     |
| `TELEGRAM_DAEMON_DEST`     | `--dest`                | Destination path for downloaded files                       | `/telegram-downloads` |
| `TELEGRAM_DAEMON_TEMP`     | `--temp`                | Destination path for temporary (download in progress) files                       | use --dest |
| `TELEGRAM_DAEMON_CHANNEL`  | `--channel`             | Channel id to download from it (Please, check [Issue 45](https://github.com/alfem/telegram-download-daemon/issues/45), [Issue 48](https://github.com/alfem/telegram-download-daemon/issues/48) and [Issue 73](https://github.com/alfem/telegram-download-daemon/issues/73))                              |                     |

| `TELEGRAM_DAEMON_TEMP`     | `--temp`                | Destination path for temporary (download in progress) files                       | use --dest |
| `TELEGRAM_DAEMON_CHANNEL`  | `--channel`             | Channel id to download from it (Please, check [Issue 45](https://github.com/alfem/telegram-download-daemon/issues/45), [Issue 48](https://github.com/alfem/telegram-download-daemon/issues/48) and [Issue 73](https://github.com/alfem/telegram-download-daemon/issues/73))                              |                     |
| `TELEGRAM_DAEMON_DUPLICATES`  | `--duplicates`             | What to do with duplicated files: ignore, overwrite or rename them | rename                     |
| `TELEGRAM_DAEMON_WORKERS`  | `--workers`             | Number of simultaneous downloads | Equals to processor cores                     |

You can define them as Environment Variables, or put them as a command line arguments, for example:

You can define them as Environment Variables, or put them as a command line arguments, for example:

    python telegram-download-daemon.py --api-id <your-id> --api-hash <your-hash> --channel <channel-number>


Finally, resend any file link to the channel to start the downloading. This daemon can manage many downloads simultaneously.

issues.title: [BUG] chat list --sort date orders by message id, not by date
issues.body:
## Description

`tlgr chat list --sort date` does not order chats by the time of their last message. `_sorted()` in `tlgr/ops/chat.py` sorts by `top_message_id`:

```python
if how == "date":
    return sorted(items, key=lambda d: -(d.top_message_id or 0))
```

Message ids are not comparable across chats. Private chats and basic groups share one per-account counter, while every channel/supergroup has its own counter. So a private chat almost always sorts above a supergroup or channel, whatever the actual dates are.

A second, smaller issue: `--limit 5` returned 6 rows (an extra pinned dialog), with or without `--sort`.

## Steps to Reproduce

```
tlgr chat list --sort date --limit 5 --json --results-only
```

## Expected Behavior

Rows ordered by `last_message.date` (newest first), and at most `--limit` rows.

## Actual Behavior

Anonymized output (`kind`, `top_message_id`, `last_message.date_unix`, `pinned`):

```
('user',       1509799, 1792184918, False)
('supergroup',  206794, 1792184899, False)
('supergroup',   29979, 1792184891, False)
('channel',      19907, 1792185309, False)   <- newest message, ranked 4th
('supergroup',     265, 1792154529, True)    <- ~8h older, ranked above the next row
('supergroup',     175, 1792184558, False)
```

6 rows for `--limit 5`.

## Suggested fix

Sort by the last message's date, e.g.:

```python
if how == "date":
    return sorted(items, key=lambda d: d.last_message.date if d.last_message else datetime.min.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc), reverse=True)
```

(or whatever the `Dialog` model's date field is). Also note that on the non-`--all` path the sort is applied only to the fetched page, so it reorders within one page rather than across all dialogs. That may be worth documenting.

## Environment

- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.4, arm64)

### Description
When downloading two documents that have identical content (same name, size, and bytes) but different remote file IDs, the second file never receives an updateFile with is_downloading_completed=true. However, calling getFile shows the file is actually downloaded.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Have two messages with documents that have identical content but were uploaded separately (different remote.unique_id)
2. Call `downloadFile` for the first document → works correctly, receive `updateFile` with `is_downloading_completed=true`
3. Call `downloadFile` for the second document → never receive `updateFile` with `is_downloading_completed=true`
4. Call getFile for the second document → shows is_downloading_completed=true

### Example
#### First file (works correctly):
```
updateFile: file_id=100, is_downloading_completed=true, remote.unique_id="AAA111"
```
#### Second file (broken):
```
updateFile: file_id=200, is_downloading_active=true, is_downloading_completed=false, remote.unique_id="BBB222"
// No further updateFile received
getFile(200): is_downloading_completed=true, remote.unique_id="AAA111"  // Note: unique_id changed after merge
```

issues.title: TDLib uses an unexpected method for inputWebFileAudioAlbumThumbLocation in normal chats
issues.body:
According to the Telegram API documentation for `inputWebFileAudioAlbumThumbLocation`, when downloading an album cover for an audio file in a normal chat, TDLib should provide the `document` field.

The `title` and `performer` fields are intended for Secret Chats and should not be used instead of `document` in normal chats.

However, TDLib currently generates `inputWebFileAudioAlbumThumbLocation` using `title` and `performer` for audio files in normal chats.

For example, TDLib generates:

```text id="4v3s8k"
inputWebFileAudioAlbumThumbLocation {
    title = "进阶"
    performer = "林俊杰"
}
```

instead of passing the `document` corresponding to the audio file.

The request then fails with:

```text id="j1h8cs"
400 : WEBFILE_NOT_AVAILABLE
```

This appears to be caused by TDLib passing the wrong fields for normal chats.

According to the Telegram API documentation, the expected behavior is:

* **Normal chats:** provide `document`
* **Secret Chats:** do not provide `document`; use `title` and `performer`

Could TDLib be updated to pass the original audio `document` when generating `inputWebFileAudioAlbumThumbLocation` for normal chats?

issues.title: Intermittent getFile response-header timeouts during 01:00–01:30 UTC since October 19, 2026, including via Alibaba Cloud GA
issues.body:
Title: Intermittent getFile response-header timeouts during 01:00–01:30 UTC since October 19, 2026, including via Alibaba Cloud GA

We have been experiencing recurring getFile timeouts since October 19, 2026.

Environment

  • Hosted Telegram Bot API: https://api.telegram.org

  • Go application running on Alibaba Cloud in Hong Kong

  • HTTP client timeout: 30 seconds per attempt

  • No application, deployment, network, or scheduled-task configuration changes around the start of the issue

  • Low application concurrency and server load during the affected period

Symptoms

The failures occur around 09:00–09:30 Asia/Shanghai (01:00–01:30 UTC). Normal operation resumes after approximately 09:30.

The recurring error is:

Post "https://api.telegram.org/bot<REDACTED>/getFile":
context deadline exceeded
(Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)

For example, failures were logged on October 22 at 09:32–09:34 and October 24 at 09:26, UTC+8, so the affected window is approximate.

issues.title: FCM push notifications delivered at "normal" priority for third-party (custom api_id) clients — delayed delivery when device is idle/locked
issues.body:
## Summary

Push notifications for messages sent to Android apps built with TDLib using a **custom `api_id`/`api_hash`** (obtained via my.telegram.org, not the official Telegram app's credentials) appear to be delivered via FCM at **"normal" priority** rather than **"high" priority**. As a result, on a locked/idle device (Android Doze mode active), delivery can be delayed anywhere from under a minute to 10+ minutes. The same messages are delivered instantly when the device is charging (Doze inactive) or when the screen is on.

This does **not** happen with the official Telegram Android app, nor with other apps that correctly mark their FCM messages as high priority (WhatsApp, Signal, Messenger, Viber — and SMS, which doesn't use FCM at all).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Register a device for push notifications via `registerDevice` with `deviceTokenFirebaseCloudMessaging`, using a Firebase project whose Service Account JSON has been uploaded to the app's config page on my.telegram.org (required to clear the `APP_PUSH_APIKEY_MISSING` error).
2. Confirm `registerDevice` succeeds (a valid `PushReceiverId` is returned).
3. Lock the device screen, unplug it from any charger, and leave it untouched for several minutes (long enough for Android to enter Doze mode).
4. Send a message to the account from another Telegram client.
5. Observe: the push often does not arrive for several minutes. Once the screen is unlocked (or the device is plugged in), any pending notification arrives immediately.

## What I've verified

- This is **not** a registration failure — `registerDevice` succeeds and `processPushNotification` successfully decrypts and processes the payload once it does arrive.

issues.title: Patch updates break API and ABI compatibility
issues.body:
Currently, `TDLib` uses only patch version increments (`1.8.x`) for all updates, but these updates regularly contain breaking `API` and `ABI` changes. This causes significant issues for the ecosystem.

### Example: `td_api.tl` breaking change in patch version
Between `1.8.52` and `1.8.53` (a patch version increment), the client-server `API` was broken:
Version `1.8.52`:
```
upgradedGiftOriginResale star_count:int53 = UpgradedGiftOrigin;
```
Version `1.8.53`:
```
upgradedGiftOriginResale price:GiftResalePrice = UpgradedGiftOrigin;
```

This change:
- Replaces `star_count:int53` with `price:GiftResalePrice`.
- Changes both the field name and type.
- Breaks binary compatibility: compiled code using `1.8.52` will crash at runtime with `1.8.53`.
- Breaks source compatibility: code must be modified and recompiled.

### Impact on different languages
For languages with compiled bindings:
- `Java`: `TdApi.java` generated classes become incompatible.
- `Rust`: `FFI` bindings fail at runtime.
- `Go`: struct definitions no longer match.

### Real-world consequences
- Production failures: applications using `1.8.52` in package managers automatically update to `1.8.53` and crash.
- Cannot receive bug fixes: users must pin exact versions (`1.8.52`), missing actual bug fixes in later patches.
- Dependency conflicts: different libraries require different "patch" versions that are actually incompatible.

### Semantic versioning as a solution
Following [semver.org](https://semver.org), this change should have been:
- `1.8.52` → `2.0.0` version when you make incompatible `API` changes.
- `1.8.52` → `1.9.0` version when you add functionality in a backward-compatible manner.
- `1.8.52` → `1.8.53` version when you make backward-compatible bug fixes.

issues.title: Personal (contact) profile photos can't be downloaded: inputPeerPhotoFileLocation returns FILE_ID_INVALID after FILE_MIGRATE
issues.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #3604. The `FILE_MIGRATE_` handling added for #3604 works: avatar downloads for personal photos (photos set via `setUserPersonalProfilePhoto`) are now resent to the DC from the error. But the resent request still fails, so these avatars only ever show the minithumbnail (the blurry preview).

For a personal photo, the server rejects `inputPeerPhotoFileLocation(peer, photo_id)` on every DC: the DC in `userProfilePhoto.dc_id` answers `FILE_MIGRATE_N`, and DC N answers `400 FILE_ID_INVALID`. `inputPhotoFileLocation(id, access_hash, file_reference, 'a'/'c')` for the same photo, taken from `userFull.personal_photo`, downloads fine from DC N.

TDLib always uses the peer form for `ProfilePhoto.small/big`, including when it has the full personal `Photo`, and it can't recover:

1. `as_dialog_photo()` (DialogPhoto.cpp) re-registers the full photo's `'a'`/`'c'` sizes with a `PhotoSizeSource::dialog_photo` source, which turns them back into `inputPeerPhotoFileLocation`.
2. After `FILE_ID_INVALID`, `FileReferenceManager::reload_photo()` calls `reload_dialog_info()`, i.e. `users.getUsers`. That returns the same `userProfilePhoto`, so the download fails again with `FILE_DOWNLOAD_ID_INVALID`, indefinitely.

## Environment

- Unigram 12.10.7 (bundles TDLib 1.8.67, includes the #3604 change), Windows 11

issues.title: One Bot vs. Multiple Bots for a Large Posting Service
issues.body:
# Scaling one Telegram bot for a large posting service

Hi!

I'm developing a long-term SaaS for scheduled Telegram posting.

Currently our architecture is:

`Main bot → separate bot per user → user's channels`

We're considering switching new users to:

`One main bot → many users → many channels`

Existing user bots could remain for compatibility.

Many Telegram posting services use separate user bots, while some use a single main bot — for example, **PostBot (~3.3M monthly users)**.

I'd like to ask Telegram/TDLib developers:

**1. Limits and scaling:**
Are there any global or per-bot rate limits specifically for publishing to many different channels, including sendMessage, copyMessage, editing and deleting messages? If burst publishing triggers 429/retry_after, is queueing/throttling the expected approach, or does Telegram recommend using multiple bot accounts for scaling?

**2. Risk of a shared bot:**
If thousands of users and channels use the same bot, can bad behavior by one user lead to restrictions or a ban of the **entire bot account**, affecting all other users?

We are **not considering Paid Broadcasts or paying for higher limits**. We're interested in the normal Bot API limits and recommended architecture.

Thanks!

issues.title: Forwarding messages into forum topics requires low-level RPC (`top_msg_id` not exposed in high-level API)
issues.body:
### Describe your suggested feature

## Environment
- **Telethon version:** 1.42.x  
- **Telegram feature:** Forum Topics (groups/channels with `forum = true`)  
- **API layer:** MTProto  
- **Client type:** User account (non-bot)

---

## Summary

Forwarding messages into a specific **forum topic** is not reliably possible using Telethon’s high-level API (`client.forward_messages`).  
Correct topic placement requires passing the protocol-level topic anchor (`top_msg_id`) via `InputReplyToMessage`, which is currently **not exposed** by the high-level helper.

As a result, forwarded messages often appear in **General** instead of the intended topic, even when replying to a placeholder message inside the topic.

---

## Background / Terminology

- **topic.id**  
  UI-level identifier shown in Telegram clients

- **top_message**  
  Message ID of the topic anchor (protocol-level, required for routing)

- **Important:**  
  `topic.id ≠ top_message`  
  Only `top_message` reliably identifies a forum topic at the protocol level.

---

## Actual Behavior

Using:

```python
await client.forward_messages(
    entity=target_chat,
    messages=source_message_id,
    from_peer=source_chat,
    reply_to=placeholder_message_id
)
```
Results in:
- The forwarded message appearing in **General**
- Even if `placeholder_message_id` is a message inside the target topic
- Even if the topic already exists and is active

This behavior is reproducible and deterministic.

---

## Expected Behavior

It should be possible to forward a message **into a specific forum topic** using Telethon, in a way that:

- Reliably places the forwarded message inside the target topic
- Does not require undocumented protocol knowledge
- Is achievable via a documented API surface (high-level or documented low-leve

"""
Minimal reproduction of race condition in MTProtoSender when used with Textual.

            print("connect() OK") # Hangs if bug present
            me = await client.get_me()  
            print(f"get_me() returned: {me}")

            await client.disconnect()
        self.exit()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    TestApp().run(headless=True)
```

When `client.connect()` is called:

2. When these loops start executing, `_user_connected` should already be `True`

**Reproduction steps:**

issues.body:
# [DEBUG] telethon.client.updates: Timeout waiting for updates expired

### Expected behavior

Telethon should continue to handle updates and respond to API requests (such as `get_me()`, `send_message()`, etc.) even after periods of inactivity or high message traffic.

Specifically, seeing the log line:

[DEBUG] telethon.client.updates: Timeout waiting for updates expired


…should not cause the client to stop processing further updates or become unresponsive.

### Reproduction steps

Unfortunately, I don’t have a minimal script yet, but here’s the general setup:

1. Create a Telethon client connected to a user or bot account.
2. Start `py-tgcalls` for group voice streaming (running on the same event loop).
3. Let the bot run for ~30–60 minutes in a moderately active chat.
4. Eventually, the above log message starts repeating.
5. After that, the bot no longer responds to any Telethon API calls, even though the event loop is still running.

A restart of the process restores normal behavior temporarily.


### Actual behavior

### Summary

I'm encountering an issue where Telethon becomes unresponsive and stops handling further API requests after repeatedly logging the following debug message:

Once this message starts appearing, my bot no longer responds to any Telethon operations — including `get_me()`, `send_message()`, and even `get_dialogs()`. The only solution is to restart the process.

### Context

I'm using Telethon along with `py-tgcalls` (for group voice streaming). The issue typically appears after some runtime (30–60 minutes), especially under higher load or activity.

> Elegant, modern and asynchronous Telegram MTProto API framework in Python for users and bots

Kurigram is an actively maintained pyrogram fork for Python designed as a drop-in replacement for Pyrogram, Kurigram provides support for the latest Telegram features including Gifts, Stories, Topics, Business Accounts, and more.

```python
from pyrogram import Client, filters

```

**Kurigram** is a modern, elegant and asynchronous [MTProto API](https://docs.kurigram.icu/topics/mtproto-vs-botapi)
framework. It enables you to easily interact with the main Telegram API through a user account (custom client) or a bot
identity (bot API alternative) using Python.

issues.title: filters.command(): command names interpolated into regex without escaping - false matches and re.error crashes
issues.body:
## Summary

`filters.command()` interpolates the user-supplied command name directly into two regular expressions without `re.escape()`. Any command containing a regex metacharacter (`.` `+` `?` `(` `[` etc.) either silently matches messages it must not match, or raises `re.error` during update dispatch.

The same applies to the follow-up `re.sub()` that strips the command from the text to build `message.command`, so arguments are also extracted incorrectly for such commands.

*Note: this is a static analysis finding based on reading the `dev` branch; no runtime execution was performed.*

## Location

- File: `pyrogram/filters.py`
- Function: `command()` (inner `func`)
- Relevant code path:

```python
for cmd in flt.commands:
    if not re.match(rf"^(?:{cmd}(?:@?{username})?)(?:\s|$)", without_prefix,
                    flags=re.IGNORECASE if not flt.case_sensitive else 0):
        continue

    without_command = re.sub(rf"{cmd}(?:@?{username})?\s?", "", without_prefix, count=1, ...)
```

## Problem

The documented parameter is a plain command name (`commands (str | list): The command or list of commands as string`), but the string is embedded in a pattern as raw regex source:

1. Metacharacters alter matching semantics. For `filters.command("buy.now")`, the compiled intent is literal `buy.now`, but the executed pattern `^(?:buy.now(?:@?mybot)?)(?:\s|$)` matches `/buyXnow`, `/buy-now`, `/buynow2`… because `.` matches any character.
2. Quantifier-bearing commands produce broader false matches. For `"c++"`, the effective pattern means "one-or-more of one-or-more `c`", so `/cc` and `/cccc` trigger the `c++` handler.
3. Some inputs make the pattern invalid. For `"what?"`, compiling `^(?:what?(?:@?user)?)(?:\s|$)` succeeds (`t?` quantifies the `t`) and then matches `/wha`,

issues.title: search_messages_count overcounts messages when from_user is specified
issues.body:
### Description

`Client.search_messages_count()` can return a count much larger than the count shown by Telegram Desktop for the same chat, user, and empty message filter.

### Reproduction

```python
from pyrogram import enums

count = await app.search_messages_count(
    chat_id=chat_id,
    from_user=me.id,
    filter=enums.MessagesFilter.EMPTY,
)
print(count)
```

Observed in a supergroup:

```text
Telegram Desktop: 8396 messages found
Kurigram:          25221
```

The Telegram Desktop search used the same chat and the same `From: <user>` filter. The result is approximately three times the expected count, which suggests that overlapping search results are being added more than once.

### Suspected cause

The current implementation obtains `messages.GetSplitRanges()` and sums `r.count` after invoking `messages.Search` through `InvokeWithMessagesRange` for every range. `messages.GetSplitRanges` is intended for splitting chat-history export requests. For message search, the ranges appear to overlap or the search result count is not restricted by the wrapper, causing duplicate counts.

### Proposed fix

Keep the split-range behavior for the history-count use case, but make `search_messages_count` count each matching message only once. A minimal regression test should mock multiple split ranges returning overlapping search results and assert that the final count is not the sum of duplicate counts.

The fix should preserve the behavior introduced by PR #292 for chats where a single `messages.Search` call undercounts results.

### References

- Current implementation: `pyrogram/methods/messages/search_messages_count.py`
- Related PR: #292 (`fix: chat message count in search_messages_count & get_chat_history_count`)

issues.title: 9 runtime bugs found while adding static type checking (ty)
issues.body:
## Summary

While integrating the [`ty`](https://github.com/astral-sh/ty) static type checker on a fork and progressively fixing its diagnostics one rule at a time (see the linked PR), several **genuine runtime bugs** surfaced along the way — not just missing/incorrect type annotations. Each one below is isolated in its own commit with a regression test that fails on the pre-fix code and passes after.

Filing them here on their own so they don't get lost even if the broader `ty`-adoption PR isn't something the project wants to take on right now.

## Bugs found

1. **`Client.get_boosts()` raises `TypeError` on every call**
   `pyrogram/methods/premium/get_boosts.py`
   `types.List(<generator expression that awaits MyBoost._parse()>)` — PEP 530 makes that an async generator, and `types.List` (a plain `list` subclass) can't be constructed from one. Fix: build the list with a comprehension first, then wrap the result in `types.List()`.

2. **`Client.get_top_chats()` crashes for every category except `USERS`**

issues.title: The PeerIdInvalid error was defined redundantly
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I am sure the error is coming from Kurigram's code and not elsewhere
- [x] I have searched in the issue tracker for similar bug reports, including closed ones
- [x] I ran `pip3 install -U https://github.com/KurimuzonAkuma/pyrogram/archive/dev.zip` and reproduced the issue using the latest development version

### Description

Duplicate definition of PeerIdInvalid error. Starting from version 2.2.5, PeerIdInvalid is defined in both 'bad_request' and 'forbidden' error categories. This caused the code that previously caught `BadRequest` to fail. According to the import order in `__init__.py`, `PeerIdInvalid(BadRequest)` was directly overwritten by `PeerIdInvalid(Forbidden)`.: 
```py
from .bad_request_400 import *
from .unauthorized_401 import *
from .service_unavailable_503 import *
from .not_acceptable_406 import *
from .flood_420 import *
from .see_other_303 import *
from .forbidden_403 import *
from .internal_server_error_500 import *

```py
from pyrogram.errors import PeerIdInvalid

try:

except KeyError:

from pyrogram import errors

try:

issues.title: handle_updates() fills updates_queue with no consumer when only connect() is used, causing unbounded memory growth
issues.body:
`Client.handle_updates()` unconditionally pushes every incoming update into `self.dispatcher.updates_queue` via `put_nowait()` (client.py, lines 960, 980, 991 and 993), with no check that anything will ever consume that queue. This causes an unbounded memory buildup in a common scenario.

**Root cause**

`Dispatcher.start()` (dispatcher.py, `start()` method) is what spawns the `handler_worker` tasks that actually drain `updates_queue` via `.get()`. It is only called from `Client.initialize()` (methods/auth/initialize.py), which is only called from `Client.start()` (methods/utilities/start.py, at the end of the method).

`Client.connect()` (methods/auth/connect.py) does **not** call `initialize()` at all. So an application that only calls `connect()` (a common pattern for scripts that just need raw API calls / a bare session, without the handler/plugin machinery) never has any `handler_worker` task running.

Despite that, `Session` keeps invoking `client.handle_updates()` for every unsolicited update coming from Telegram (`session.py`, `self._create_tracked_task(self.client.handle_updates(msg.body))`), regardless of whether the Dispatcher was ever started. `handle_updates()` then keeps calling `updates_queue.put_nowait(...)` unconditionally. Since nothing ever calls `.get()` on that `asyncio.Queue` in this scenario, it grows without bound for the entire lifetime of the connection - a real memory leak with zero benefit.

**Why `no_updates=True` doesn't solve this**

`no_updates=True` wraps every outgoing request in `InvokeWithoutUpdates` (methods/advanced/invoke.py), which tells *Telegram* to stop sending updates altogether. That's not always what's wanted: an application may need Telegram to keep sending updates (e.g. to keep local `pts`/`qts` state current, or to consum

issues.title: Shape-dependent methods do not type-check: `download_media()` rejects its own documented call, six others never narrow
issues.body:
### Checklist
- [x] I am sure the error is coming from Kurigram's code and not elsewhere
- [x] I have searched in the issue tracker for similar bug reports, including closed ones
- [x] I reproduced the issue using the latest development version

Verified on `dev` at `28a7e31` with `mypy 2.3.0` on `Python 3.14`.

### Description

Seven public methods return different types depending on their arguments. The caller always knows which case they asked for; the annotations do not express it. `get_messages` already does this correctly with overloads, so the library contains its own reference implementation.

**Part 1 — `download_media()` has overloads, and they reject the plain call.**

Each of the three overloads added in #275 requires a keyword argument that has no default:

| overload | required keyword | returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `block: Literal[False]` | `None` |
| 2 | `in_memory: Literal[True]` | `BinaryIO \| List[BinaryIO]` |
| 3 | `in_memory: Literal[False]` | `str \| List[str]` |

So `download_media(message)` matches nothing and falls back to `Any` — and that call is the first example in the method's own docstring:

```python
# Download from Message
await app.download_media(message)
```

`download_media(message, file_name="downloads/")` does not match either. Neither does `download_media(message, "downloads/", True)`, which is legal at runtime because the implementation signature takes `in_memory` and `block` positionally while the overloads declare them keyword-only.

The discriminator is the wrong parameter, too. `block` decides whether a value comes back at all; `in_memory` only picks which value. Overloads 2 and 3 both leave `block: bool = True`, claiming a return value for `block=False`, and so overlap overload 1, which says `None` for that same call.

issues.title: get_dialogs() raises AttributeError on a chat with direct messages enabled
issues.body:
## What happens

Enabling direct messages on any channel the account can see takes out `get_dialogs()` for the
whole account:

```python
async for dialog in app.get_dialogs():
    ...
# -> AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'user_id'
#    pyrogram/types/messages_and_media/message.py:1862
```

It is not one dialog that comes back wrong — the exception leaves the generator, so the listing
stops at whatever position that chat happens to occupy and nothing after it is ever yielded. No
argument to `get_dialogs()` avoids it.

## Why

`Message._parse_message()` reads `saved_peer_id` unguarded on the direct-messages branch
(`message.py:1861-1864` on `dev`):

```python
if chat.type == enums.ChatType.DIRECT:
    parsed_message.direct_messages_topic_id = message.saved_peer_id.user_id

    parsed_topic = client.topic_cache[(parsed_message.chat.id, parsed_message.direct_messages_topic_id)]
```

The field is optional in the schema (`compiler/api/source/main_api.tl:133`):

```
message#7600b9d3 ... peer_id:Peer saved_peer_id:flags.28?Peer ...
```

So a message in such a chat that carries no topic arrives without it, and `.user_id` is read off
`None`.

`get_dialogs()` parses the last message of every dialog, which is how one message in one chat
reaches every caller of the method.

Related, and probably the same fix: `messageService#7a800e0a` declares `saved_peer_id:flags.28?Peer`
too (`main_api.tl:134`), but service messages go through `_parse_service()`, which never looks at
it. They cannot crash here — they also never get a `direct_messages_topic_id` at all, so a reply
built from one loses the topic.

## Reproduce

No account and no network needed — one raw message with the flag absent, handed straight to the
parser. Save as `repro.py`, run it from a checkout of `dev`:

issues.title: handle_updates: PERSISTENT_TIMESTAMP_OUTDATED on GetChannelDifference escapes as TimeoutError and drops the whole update batch
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I am sure the error is coming from Kurigram's code and not elsewhere
- [x] I have searched in the issue tracker for similar bug reports, including closed ones
- [ ] I ran the latest development version and reproduced the issue — **not reproduced on `dev`**: the trigger is a transient Telegram server error that cannot be provoked on demand. I did compare the code instead: the relevant parts of `pyrogram/client.py` (`handle_updates`) and `pyrogram/session/session.py` (`Session.invoke`) are unchanged on `dev`.

### Description

`Client.handle_updates` enriches an `UpdateNewChannelMessage` that carries min peers by calling `updates.GetChannelDifference`. That call is wrapped in

```python
except (ChannelPrivate, PersistentTimestampOutdated, PersistentTimestampInvalid):
    pass
```

so a `PERSISTENT_TIMESTAMP_OUTDATED` is meant to be tolerated. But that `except` never fires for it:

1. `PersistentTimestampOutdated` is a subclass of `InternalServerError` (500).
2. `Session.invoke` catches `InternalServerError` and retries (`except (OSError, InternalServerError, ServiceUnavailable)`).
3. After `MAX_RETRIES` attempts it raises a plain `TimeoutError(f'Failed to invoke "{query_name}" after {retries} retries')`. The original RPC error is gone.
4. `TimeoutError` does not match the `except` tuple in `handle_updates`, so it propagates out of the coroutine.

Because `handle_updates` runs as a tracked task (`Session._create_tracked_task`) whose result nobody awaits, the only trace is asyncio's `Task exception was never retrieved`.

The exception leaves the `for update in updates.updates:` loop mid-way:

- the triggering update is never passed to `dispatcher.updates_queue.put_nowait(...)`, so no `on_message` handler sees that

issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I am sure the error is coming from Pyrogram's code and not elsewhere
- [x] I have searched in the issue tracker for similar bug reports, including closed ones
- [x] I ran `pip3 install -U https://github.com/pyrogram/pyrogram/archive/master.zip` and reproduced the issue using the latest development version

### Description

Hello!
I found some potential problems in the current implementation.

### Ignored bad server salt
When we send ping message, the server can respond with bad server salt message, and it will be ignored because we are not waiting for the response for Ping Message, and the code that updates salt will never be reached.
This is not a big problem, because at some point Watchdog will send getUpdateState, then will receive bad server salt in response and salt will finally be updated.
But it seems that Watchdog does not maintain media sessions, which is why they probably stop working over time.

### Persistent media sessions
Earlier, in version 2.0.106, sessions were created during the upload, and then closed.
At some point, media session reusing was implemented in kurigram, and perhaps this was done incorrectly.
Firstly, it is discouraged by telegram:

> Downloading Files and Uploading Data to the Server
We recommend that separate connections and sessions be created for these tasks. Remember that the extra sessions must be deleted when no longer needed.

[source](https://core.telegram.org/api/optimisation)
Secondly, As I understand it, salt in such sessions expires at some point, and if Session is not used within an hour, the server stops receiving messages from that session, and uploading / downloading files becomes impossible.

### Simple fix
I think if stop ignoring salt in response to Ping, these problems will be resolved.

issues.title: [Feature Request]: Add `video_cover` support to `copy_message` and `copy_media_group`
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I believe the idea is awesome and would benefit the framework
- [x] I have searched in the issue tracker for similar requests, including closed ones

### Description



    ### Feature Description

    Currently, `Client.copy_message` and `Client.copy_media_group` allow copying media without forwarding headers, but there is no way to preserve or supply custom video covers  (`video_cover`) for video media.

    When copying a video or video album, the original video cover is often lost, and there is no parameter to supply a new cover (via `file_id`, URL, or local path) without downloading and re-uploading the entire video file.

    ### Proposed Solution

    1. **`Client.copy_message`**:
       - Add parameter `video_cover: str | PathLike I BinaryIO | bool | None = None`
       - If `True`: preserve the existing video
       cover from the original message.
       - If `False`: strip the cover.
       - If `str` (`file_id`, URL, or file path) or  `BinaryIO`: upload/attach the custom cover using `raw.types.InputMediaUploadedPhoto` / `InputMediaPhotoExternal` or  `utils.get_input_media_from_file_id`, and map it to `raw.types.InputMediaDocument.video_cover`.

    2. **`Client.copy_media_group`**:
       - Add parameter `video_covers: list[str |  PathLike | BinaryIO | bool] | str | PathLike | BinaryIO | bool = True`
       - Allow passing a list of covers matching the items in the media group, or a boolean to preserve/strip covers across the group.

    ### Use Case
    Bots that organize, mirror, or deliver video albums often need to apply custom covers or maintain HD covers without incurring the huge bandwidth and CPU overhead of re-uploading entire multi-gigabyte video files.

issues.title: AnimatedChatPhoto._parse raises ValueError for sticker profile photos
issues.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I am sure the error is coming from Kurigram's code and not elsewhere
- [x] I have searched in the issue tracker for similar bug reports, including closed ones
- [x] I ran `pip3 install -U https://github.com/KurimuzonAkuma/pyrogram/archive/dev.zip` and reproduced the issue using the latest development version

## Description

`AnimatedChatPhoto._parse()` raises `ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty` when `photo.video_sizes` is non-empty but contains only `VideoSizeEmojiMarkup` or `VideoSizeStickerMarkup` entries.

This is a valid Telegram API representation for sticker/custom-emoji profile pictures. `VideoSize` is a union of `videoSize`, `videoSizeEmojiMarkup`, and `videoSizeStickerMarkup`. The current parser checks only whether `photo.video_sizes` itself is empty, then filters for concrete `raw.types.VideoSize` instances and calls `max()` without checking whether the filtered list is empty.

This can make `Client.get_chat()` fail for a user or bot using a sticker/custom-emoji profile picture. It also prevents the subsequent `ChatPhotoSticker._parse()` call from handling the markup entry.

Reproduced with Kurigram 2.2.25 from the latest `dev` branch at commit `af475ac0d427a6a1aeb924e56e951484381f1c07`, using Python 3.12.9.

Telegram schema references:

- https://core.telegram.org/type/VideoSize
- https://core.telegram.org/api/files#uploading-profile-or-chat-pictures

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install the latest development version:

issues.title: Sync user avatars automatically
issues.body: Avatar syncing is mostly disabled due to potential API call flooding. We should try to figure out a way to sync avatars when needed without causing flooding.

issues.title: Forwarded albums are only bridged as a single image
issues.body:
When an album is sent from the Telegram side, it gets correctly bridged as multiple images. When a forwarded message is sent from the Telegram side, it gets correctly sent as a message with some "forwarded from" header information.

However, when the thing being forwarded is an *album*, it will only bridge a single image, seemingly the ~~last~~ first one.

issues.title: Remove message duplication
issues.body:
Messages are duplicated a lot: If a portal room has multiple real Matrix users, messages from real Telegram users are duplicated for each real Matrix user. Messages from real Matrix users are also duplicated for each real Matrix user except for the sender.

Telegram doesn't have globally unique message IDs (only per-user unique IDs), so we have to figure out some other way to handle duplicate messages.

If #4 is implemented, we can use the bot as the primary source of information for all chats the bot has been added to. However, we'd still need to figure out how to avoid duplicates in chats without the bot.

issues.title: Images with captions don't store Matrix event ID of caption
issues.body:
Currently the database can only store one event ID per Telegram message (except for edits). However, images with captions are bridged as two messages. This means that:

* Replying to the image event from Matrix won't be bridged correctly
* Deleting the image event from Matrix won't be bridged correctly
* Deleting the message from Telegram will only delete the caption

Bridging image messages as inline images is already supported by the bridge, but not supported by most clients. The preferred solution would be implementing matrix-org/matrix-doc#2530 everywhere, but alternatively the database could be updated to support a many-to-one mapping.

issues.title: Support blocking all topics in a Telegram forum via portal creation filter
issues.body:
The current "portal_create_filter" in mautrix-telegram (Go / bridgev2) only supports exact portal ID matching.

For Telegram forum groups, each topic has a separate portal ID:

```
channel:123456789:-1    # Forum space
channel:123456789       # General
channel:123456789:456   # Topic A
channel:123456789:789   # Topic B
```

Adding the parent group to the deny list:

```
filter deny channel:123456789
```

does not prevent individual topic portals from being created.

This is particularly problematic for large, active Telegram forums where new topics are created frequently. Users must continually add each new topic to the deny list, or switch to an allowlist that also blocks unrelated chats.

In my case, the forum is read-only, and its topics do not bridge messages correctly, but the bridge keeps creating Matrix rooms for new topics.

Proposed solution

Allow a filter entry for a parent Telegram forum to match all its child topic portals, including topics created in the future.

For example, introduce a "recursive" option:

```
bridge:
  portal_create_filter:
    mode: deny
    list:
      - id: "channel:123456789"
        recursive: true
```

This should block portal creation for all topics belonging to the specified Telegram forum while leaving other Telegram chats unaffected.

Ideally, the behavior should also be available through the "filter" management command.

Expected behavior

- Users can exclude an entire Telegram forum and all its present and future topics from automatic Matrix portal creation.
- Other Telegram chats continue bridging normally.
- Existing portals are not deleted automatically.
- Users do not need to leave or mute the Telegram forum itself.

Additional context

Related issue: #1084 (Forum topic portals created in database but no Matrix rooms).

issues.title: Client stays up forever after "engine was closed"; no reconnect, unit never exits
issues.body:
**Version:** mautrix-telegram v0.2609.0 (Go/bridgev2), built from the tag with
`-tags goolm`, Go 1.26.7, Linux x86_64 (NixOS), Synapse 1.154, PostgreSQL 16.
Single user login, ~220 portals.

## What happens

After a connection problem, the vendored gotd client's RPC engine is closed,
and from then on every request fails with `engine was closed`:

```
error | Failed to get difference, retrying in 5 seconds... | component=telegram_client error="engine was closed"
error | get channel difference error | component=telegram_client error="get channel difference: engine was closed"
```

These repeat every few seconds indefinitely (about 7,500 lines in 6 h). No
reconnect happens, nothing is bridged any more, and the process neither
exits nor logs `Client exited ...` / `Update manager exited ...`, so a
supervisor (systemd `Restart=on-failure`) never restarts it. Only a manual
restart recovers.

Seen twice in one day:

1. After ~13 h of normal operation:
   ```
   10:02:02 warn  Acknowledge timed out, performing retry
   10:02:02 error Retry failed  error="write: write intermediate: write tcp ...:443: write: broken pipe"

   No error preceded it at info level: last normal line 18:05:30, then at
   18:12:39 the `engine was closed` loop started. The process then had no TCP

issues.title: Feature: Skip already downloaded files instead of renaming & re-downloading
issues.body:
Problem:

Currently when a file already exists, the downloader creates a new name (file_1.mp4, file_2.mp4...) and downloads it again. This wastes bandwidth and creates duplicate files.

Solution:

I modified the download_media function so that if the file already exists in the download directory, it simply skips it and moves to the next message.Change made in download_media function:

if _is_exist(file_name):
    logger.info("File already exists, skipping - %s", file_name)
    DOWNLOADED_IDS[chat_id].append(message.id)
    PROCESSED_IDS[chat_id].append(message.id)
    return message.id

issues.body:
Telethon is slow when uploading files because it does so by uploading the file chunks sequentially, rather than in parallel, how the pyrogram does. The telethon developer has no interest in changing this. Uploading with pyrogram is 5–10 times faster than using telethon.

Also, the pyrogram code is much simpler and easier to work with. Rather than using hacks like fastTelethon, this solution is an alternative to #140 and resolves the low speed by default.

readme_amostras.texto:
you probably know what you're doing anyway :)

Slow downloads?
---------------

You may also want to install ``cryptg`` with the same method for a speed

You may also want to install ``cryptg`` with the same method for a speed
boost when downloading media. Telegram requires a lot of encryption and
decryption and this can make downloading files especially slow unless
using a nice fast library like cryptg. One user reported a `speed
increase of
1100% <https://github.com/expectocode/telegram-export/issues/29>`__.

It uses the Telegram API (what Telegram apps use), so it has access to
everything a Telegram app can do. This is why you need an API ID and API
hash to use it, and why one from Telegram Desktop will work. Since
normal clients need to download messages, media, users etc to display
them in-app, telegram-export can do the same, and save them into a nice
database.

So no, it's not really a bot, but it does use the same technology as
**userbots** in order to work. As far as we know, it won't get you banned from
using Telegram or anything like that.

Installation from source

issues.title: Unsafe chat names when downloading media
issues.body:
Some chat names, eg. "a/b/c", when using with
`MediaFilenameFmt = usermedia/{name}-{context_id}/{type}-{filename}`
can create folders like "usermedia/a/b/c--123456/document-filename.123.txt"

This is not intended and unsafe (like `a/../../b`), and also have problems with other filesystem filename restrictions. Please really sanitize the chat name, sender name and file names. For example, replace `" * / : < > ? \ |` characters with `_`.

issues.title: Bot hangs (zombie state) instead of crashing on TimeoutException in updates.getChannelDifference
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
When a `TimeoutException` occurs during `updates.getChannelDifference`, the background update-polling fiber crashes and stops fetching new updates entirely. 
However, the main EventLoop and outbound connections remain alive (the bot can still catch the exception and send error messages to a Telegram chat). The core issue is that MadelineProto does not automatically recover or restart the update loop after this specific timeout, leaving the bot deaf to new updates until manually restarted via `$this->restart()`.

**To Reproduce**
It happens randomly due to network timeouts when the bot tries to fetch updates via `updates.getChannelDifference`.

**Expected behavior**
MadelineProto should catch the timeout internally and retry fetching updates, or automatically restart the polling fiber, rather than letting the update loop die while the rest of the bot stays alive.

include 'madeline.php';

or

issues.title: [Bug]: FloodWait during auth.ExportAuthorization is not respected, causing repeated download failures
issues.body:
### Summary

When Telegram returns a `FloodWait` exception during `auth.ExportAuthorization`, Telegram Media Downloader does not wait for the required duration.  Instead, the application treats the exception as a stale file reference, retries after only 2 seconds, and eventually marks the download as failed.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Telegram Media Downloader in Docker with multiple Telegram channels.
2. Enable daemon mode and download history tracking.
3. Start downloading a large number of documents from channel history.
4. Continue until Telegram returns `FloodWait` during `auth.ExportAuthorization`.
5. Observe how the downloader handles the exception.

### Expected Behavior

- Detect `pyrogram.errors.FloodWait`.
- Pause downloading for the duration specified by Telegram (`e.value`), preferably with a small safety margin.
- Avoid processing additional downloads while the rate limit is active.
- Resume the current download after the waiting period.
- Do not mark a download as failed solely because Telegram temporarily requires a cooldown.

### Actual Behavior

- Telegram returns `FloodWait` requesting a wait of approximately 268 seconds.
- The downloader logs `Stale file reference`.
- It retries after 2 seconds instead of respecting the requested waiting period.
- After two retries, the file is marked as failed.
- The downloader immediately attempts the next file and encounters the same error.

### Version

v1.4.0

### Deployment Environment

Docker (Linux)

### Relevant Logs

```shell
Telegram says: [420 FLOOD_WAIT_X] - A wait of 268 seconds is required
(caused by "auth.ExportAuthorization")

pyrogram.errors.exceptions.flood_420.FloodWait:
Telegram says: [420 FLOOD_WAIT_X] - A wait of 268 seconds is required

[ERROR] Download produced empty file after 2 r

issues.title: Auth session expiry is invisible - crash-loops silently instead of alerting
issues.body:
Ran into this live: the container's Telegram session got revoked (`401 AUTH_KEY_UNREGISTERED`) and it crash-looped every ~60s for 5 days straight (962 restarts) before I noticed, purely by chance. Nothing surfaced it - no Discord ping, no obviously-unhealthy container in `docker ps`, nothing.

**Why it's invisible right now:**

- The fatal auth error is only caught by the top-level `except Exception` in `__main__` (`src/main.py`), which just prints to stderr and calls `sys.exit(1)`. It never reaches the `NotificationManager` that already exists in the codebase (`src/notifications/`, Discord + generic webhook support) - that's only wired up inside `main()`'s daemon path, not the outer crash handler.
- `HealthMonitor` (`src/daemon/health.py`) never gets a chance to write `status=error` either, for the same reason - the process dies before any of that runs.
- Docker's own HEALTHCHECK (`healthcheck.py`) checks health-file *staleness* (`MAX_AGE_SECONDS=600`), but a crash-loop restarts fast enough that a fresh `starting` status gets written well inside that window every cycle. So the container never sits "unhealthy" long enough to look wrong in `docker ps` - it just looks like it's permanently starting.
- End result: an auth failure and a container that's merely slow to warm up look identical from the outside, and the one that actually matters is the one that never gets fixed.

**What I'd want instead:**

1. Catch Telegram auth errors specifically (`AuthKeyUnregistered`, `SessionRevoked`, `UserDeactivated`, and friends) in a dedicated handler, distinct from a generic fatal error - this is a "human has to intervene" class of failure, not a transient one worth just retrying.
2. On that specific failure, write `status=error` to the health file with a reason string before exiting

issues.title: One failing source aborts the entire check iteration
issues.body:
## Description

`run_check()` iterates sources sequentially with no per-source error isolation. If scanning or fetching messages for one source raises mid-run (FloodWait bubble-up, channel deleted between startup and the check, transient RPC error), the exception aborts the whole iteration: every source after the failing one is skipped.

In daemon mode the loop retries at the next interval, but a persistently broken source starves all sources ordered after it, forever. In single-shot mode the run just dies.

Startup-time validation already skips unresolvable sources; this is the runtime counterpart.

## Proposed Behavior

- Wrap the per-source body of `run_check()` in try/except
- On failure: log the error with the source name, count it in the run summary, continue with the next source
- Keep FloodWait handling intact (the daemon's circuit breaker should still see it if every source is rate-limited - e.g. re-raise FloodWait but isolate everything else, or track and re-raise at the end of the loop)
- Notify (throttled) when a source fails repeatedly across N consecutive iterations

## Implementation Notes

- The pending-downloads queue already makes this safe: an aborted source resumes from its queue next run
- Add a `sources_failed` counter to the run summary

issues.title: feat: download scheduling and bandwidth controls
issues.body:
## Description

Add time-based scheduling and optional bandwidth throttling so users can control when and how fast downloads happen.

## Use Cases

- Download only during off-peak hours on metered connections
- Avoid saturating shared network during work hours
- Rate-limit to stay under ISP or Telegram thresholds

## Proposed Configuration

### Schedule

```yaml
# Only download during these hours (24h format, local timezone via TZ)
- TDL_SCHEDULE_ACTIVE_HOURS=02:00-08:00
```

- Outside active hours, the daemon still runs health checks but skips `run_check()`
- If a download is in progress when the window closes, let it finish (don't interrupt mid-transfer)
- Empty/unset means no restriction (current behavior)

### Bandwidth Throttling

```yaml
# Max download speed (supports KB, MB suffixes)
- TDL_MAX_DOWNLOAD_SPEED=5MB
```

- Apply throttling via Pyrogram's progress callback by introducing delays between chunks
- Alternatively, limit concurrent downloads to 1 and add a per-file rate limiter
- Empty/unset means no restriction (current behavior)

## Implementation Notes

- Schedule check goes in `DaemonService.run_check()` before calling the check function
- Log when skipping due to schedule: `"Outside active hours (02:00-08:00), skipping check"`
- Support multiple windows: `TDL_SCHEDULE_ACTIVE_HOURS=02:00-08:00,22:00-23:59`
- Handle windows that cross midnight (e.g., `23:00-06:00`)
- Bandwidth limiter should be a wrapper/decorator around the download call

issues.title: [Feature]: Persistent download tracking independent of folder contents
issues.body:
### Summary

Persistent download tracking independent of output folder contents

### Problem Statement

Currently, the tool determines whether a file has already been downloaded by checking if the file exists in the target output folder.

This creates a problem in workflows where files are automatically moved, renamed, or processed after download. If a file is moved out of the original folder (for example, into long-term storage or another directory), the downloader detects it as missing and downloads it again.

This results in:

Unnecessary re-downloads
Increased bandwidth usage
Duplicate storage consumption
Extra processing time

This mainly affects users who integrate the downloader into automated pipelines or post-processing systems (e.g., media servers, archival workflows, unionfs/mergerfs setups, etc.).

### Proposed Solution

Introduce a persistent download tracking mechanism that does not rely solely on checking the output folder.

Instead of using filesystem presence, the downloader could optionally maintain a local state database storing identifiers.

### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

_No response_

issues.title: fix: source date filters crash startup
issues.body:
Setting a date filter on a source stops that source from loading.

`build_filters` calls `DateFilter(after=..., before=...)`, but `DateFilter.__init__` takes `only_after` and `only_before`. With `TDL_SOURCES_0_FILTERS_ONLY_AFTER` or `TDL_SOURCES_0_FILTERS_ONLY_BEFORE` set (or `only_after` / `only_before` in YAML), startup fails with:

```
ConfigError: Failed to parse source 1: DateFilter.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'after'
```

Once that is fixed, `DateFilter.matches` compares Pyrogram's naive `message.date` with the aware UTC config dates and raises `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`.

The docs also name the settings `TDL_SOURCES_N_FILTERS_MIN_DATE` / `MAX_DATE`, which the loader never reads, so those are silently ignored.

issues.title: fix: config validation gaps for archives, retries, log level and detail level
issues.body:
Four config validation bugs:

1. A source with any filter set ignores the global `allow_archives`: the per-source value (default false) is always used.
2. `max_retries` accepts 0. The downloader treats it as total attempts, so 0 means no file is ever downloaded, with no error.
3. `daemon.log_level` is not checked when the config loads; a bad value crashes later in `getattr(logging, ...)`.
4. `notifications.detail_level` is accepted but never used.

issues.title: Publish an Unraid Community Applications template
issues.body:
## Description

Unraid's Community Applications store is one of the highest-leverage distribution channels for self-hosted media tooling - it is where the arr-stack audience discovers new containers, and this project is a natural fit next to Radarr/Sonarr/qBittorrent templates. Right now an Unraid user has to hand-craft the container config, including the fiddly first-run auth.

## Proposed Work

- Create an Unraid XML template: image (`rfsbraz/telegram-downloader`), `/downloads` and session/config volume mappings, PUID/PGID/TZ, and the core TDL_* variables (API credentials, sources, daemon mode) with descriptions
- Host it in a `templates/` folder or a dedicated `unraid-templates` repo (CA supports both)
- Submit to Community Applications (requires a support thread on the Unraid forums - that thread itself becomes an outreach/support channel)
- Add an "Install on Unraid" section to the README and docs site

## Implementation Notes

- Session-string auth (#60) pairs well with this: Unraid users cannot easily attach to a container for the login code, so land that first (or document the one-shot auth container flow in the template description)
- Icon: CA templates want a hosted PNG; reuse the project logo

issues.title: Dry-run mode: preview what would be downloaded
issues.body:
## Description

There is no way to validate a configuration without actually downloading. New users tuning filters (extensions, sizes, patterns, date ranges) against a large channel either download gigabytes they didn't want or comment sources in and out blindly. A dry-run mode turns the first-run experience from "hope" into "verify".

## Proposed Configuration

```yaml
- TDL_DRY_RUN=true
```

## Proposed Behavior

- Scan all sources and evaluate filters exactly as a real run would
- Log each file that WOULD download: name, size, source, destination path
- Log each file that would be skipped and why (extension, size, pattern, date, duplicate, already tracked)
- Finish with the normal run summary (count + total bytes that would transfer)
- Write nothing: no downloads, no cursor updates, no history records, no pending-queue mutations

## Implementation Notes

- Most of the plumbing exists: scan phase + filter evaluation are already separate from the download phase
- Guard `cursor_store.set`, `history.record` and `pending` mutations behind the flag (or inject no-op stores, which keeps run_check clean)
- Combine with single-shot mode for a natural `docker compose run downloader` UX; in daemon mode, log a warning that dry-run is active every iteration so it is never left on by accident

issues.title: Prometheus metrics endpoint
issues.body:
## Description

The homelab audience that runs this next to the arr stack almost universally runs Prometheus + Grafana. Exposing a small `/metrics` endpoint would make the downloader observable with zero custom tooling, and dashboards/alerts become community-shareable artifacts (outreach: Grafana dashboard on grafana.com linking back to the project).

## Proposed Metrics

```
telegram_downloader_files_downloaded_total{source="..."}
telegram_downloader_bytes_downloaded_total{source="..."}
telegram_downloader_files_failed_total{source="..."}
telegram_downloader_files_skipped_total{source="...", reason="duplicate|tracked|error"}
telegram_downloader_pending_queue_size{source="..."}
telegram_downloader_last_check_timestamp_seconds
telegram_downloader_check_duration_seconds
telegram_downloader_floodwait_seconds_total
telegram_downloader_up
```

## Proposed Configuration

```yaml
- TDL_METRICS_ENABLED=true
- TDL_METRICS_PORT=9184
```

## Implementation Notes

- `prometheus-client` is a tiny dependency and runs its own HTTP server in a thread (`start_http_server`)
- Counters map 1:1 onto the run-summary counters (#34); increment in the same places
- Off by default; document a scrape config snippet and ship a starter Grafana dashboard JSON in `docs/`

issues.title: Migrate from unmaintained Pyrogram to an actively maintained fork
issues.body:
## Description

The project pins `pyrogram>=2.0.106`, but upstream Pyrogram has been unmaintained since 2023. We are already carrying workarounds for its bugs (the `get_dialogs()` NoneType crash behind #47, silent 0-byte files on internally-handled FileReferenceExpired, stale file references). Newer Telegram API layers (larger files, new media types, forum topic improvements) will never land there, and Python 3.13+ compatibility is at risk.

## Proposed Change

Evaluate and migrate to an actively maintained fork - kurigram (`kurigram` on PyPI) is the most active drop-in candidate; pyrofork is the other contender. Both keep the `pyrogram` import path, so the migration should be mostly a dependency swap plus regression testing.

## Benefits

- Upstream fixes for the dialog-parsing crash class instead of local workarounds
- Current Telegram API layer: 4 GB file support, new chat/media types
- Python 3.13 support and active security maintenance
- Fewer FloodWait edge cases (forks have improved session handling)

## Implementation Notes

- Swap the dependency, run the full unit + integration suite
- Smoke-test against a real account: auth flow, channel/group/forum-topic sources, large file download, FloodWait behavior
- Verify session files remain compatible (both forks use the same SQLite session format) - document a re-auth path if not
- Keep the defensive workarounds for one release, remove them once the fork proves stable

projetos.descricao: Own your Telegram history. Automated, incremental backups with a local web viewer that feels just like the real app. Docker-ready and supports public chat sharing

readme_amostras.texto:
Telegram Desktop's own export is a one-off file with no earlier versions and no deleted messages; this runs on a schedule, keeps earlier versions and deleted messages, and can import that export too.

## Features

- Keeps every edit with its earlier text, and keeps every deleted message, marked as deleted, with its text and media.
- Saves photos, videos, voice notes, stickers, documents and link previews once each, however many chats share them, and skips files over a size you set.
- Reads like Telegram: chats, forum topics, folders, archived chats, reactions, pinned messages, polls and shared media, with search across every chat.
- Shows what Telegram no longer does: a What changed feed of deletions, edits and new transcripts, and the earlier profile photos of every chat.
- Backs up several accounts into one archive, and imports Telegram Desktop exports.
- Turns voice messages into searchable text through a transcription server you run or rent.

## Quick start

You need Docker Compose, and an `api_id` and `api_hash` for your account from [my.telegram.org/apps](https://my.telegram.org/apps).

```bash
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GeiserX/Telegram-Archive/main/docker-compose.yml

cat > .env <<'EOF'
TELEGRAM_API_ID=12345678
TELEGRAM_API_HASH=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
TELEGRAM_PHONE=+15551234567
VIEWER_USERNAME=admin
VIEWER_PASSWORD=choose-a-long-password

Release notes are in the [changelog](https://github.com/GeiserX/Telegram-Archive/blob/main/docs/CHANGELOG.md). Open an [issue](https://github.com/GeiserX/Telegram-Archive/issues) for bugs and questions; the [troubleshooting page](https://geiserx.github.io/Telegram-Archive/operations/troubleshooting/#reporting-a-bug) says what to include. Report security problems through the [security policy](https://github.com/GeiserX/Telegram-Archive/blob/main/SECURITY.md), never in a public issue.

issues.title: [Bug]: Large media files can never finish downloading — flood_sleep_threshold=0 turns mid-transfer FloodWaits into restarts from byte 0
issues.body:
### Version

v7.26.0 (tag `37b5c77`); re-verified at current `main` (`dc6504d`). Also reproduced on 7.7.0 (older log wording, same behavior).

### Deployment Method

Docker Compose

### Database Type

SQLite (default)

### Bug Description

Media files whose transfer takes longer than the account's current flood-free window can **never** be archived: every attempt aborts on the first mid-download `FloodWaitError` and restarts from byte 0, hits the next flood at roughly the same point, and loops until the retry budget is exhausted. The file stays `downloaded=0` ("Will download on next backup" in the viewer) forever, and after `MEDIA_MAX_DOWNLOAD_ATTEMPTS` runs it is permanently skipped. Small files are unaffected, which makes this easy to miss — the archive looks healthy except the biggest files silently never arrive.

There is no env-var workaround; the responsible setting is hardcoded.

#### Root cause

Three pieces interact:

1. **`src/config.py`** — both `build_telegram_client_kwargs()` and `Config.get_telegram_client_kwargs()` hardcode:

   ```python
   kwargs: dict = {"flood_sleep_threshold": 0}
   ```

   Introduced in #124 so flood waits surface in the app's logs instead of Telethon sleeping silently — a reasonable goal for *iteration* calls (`iter_messages` etc.), where the app's wrapper resumes from a cursor and nothing is lost.

2. **Telethon semantics** (`telethon/client/users.py::_call`): on `FLOOD_WAIT_X`, if `X <= flood_sleep_threshold` Telethon sleeps and **re-invokes the same request** — for `download_media` that means the same `upload.getFile` chunk, i.e. the transfer *resumes where it was*. With threshold `0` it always raises instead (Telethon floors `e.seconds` to 1 first, so even a 0-second flood exceeds the threshold), aborting `download_media` entir

issues.title: [Bug]: get_dialogs() never completes for accounts with enough dialogs to trip FloodWait (retry restarts pagination from scratch)
issues.body:
### Version
v7.7.0 (reproduced; confirmed the relevant `_get_dialogs()` / `call_with_flood_retry()` logic is unchanged on `main` as of this writing, v7.33.6)

### Deployment Method
Docker Compose

### Database Type
PostgreSQL

### Bug Description

On an account with a large number of dialogs (~1,900 in this case), the initial (non-whitelist) backup never completes `get_dialogs()` — it fails with the same ~25s `FloodWaitError` on every single scheduled run, no matter how far apart the runs are spaced (tested 6h apart, 4 runs, identical failure every time) or how many retries `MAX_FLOOD_RETRIES` allows (tested up to 40 consecutive retries — every one hit an essentially identical wait, no decay or jitter that would let it through).

**Root cause:** the client runs with `flood_sleep_threshold=0` (#124), so `client.get_dialogs()` — which paginates internally in ~100-dialog chunks via repeated `GetDialogsRequest` calls — aborts its *entire* call the moment any single internal page hits a FloodWait. `call_with_flood_retry` then sleeps and calls `get_dialogs()` again *from scratch*, re-walking the same already-successful early pages before hitting the same later page's FloodWait again. For an account whose dialog count requires enough pages to reliably trip a wait, this never converges — it's not cumulative account-level throttling wearing off over time (which more retries or a longer backoff would fix), it's the same deterministic wall being re-hit on every attempt.

This is the same failure class as #232 (mid-download FloodWaits restarting a media transfer from byte 0), just for `get_dialogs()` instead of media downloads. #232 was fixed via `MEDIA_FLOOD_SLEEP_THRESHOLD` / `absorb_media_floods()`, which lets Telethon absorb short floods *in place* (sleep + resume) instead of r
