- Scrolling through later days, the pill keeps showing the original date while
  the messages on screen belong to other days.
- It renders on top of the inline per-day separators, so at a day boundary two
  contradictory pills stack (screenshot: floating "May 21, 2026" covering the
  inline "July 24, 2026" separator - the viewer asserts May while July
  messages are on screen).

This may be newly visible because of the 7.29.0 detached-window work: now that
date jumps and bidirectional paging routinely make the viewed day differ from
the first-loaded day, a pill that never re-computes is wrong most of the time.

### Expected Behavior

Keep the floating date pill as a permanent, always-visible element (it's very
practical for orientation). The only fix needed: it should reflect the day of
the messages currently at the top of the viewport and update continuously as
you scroll - each time you scroll past a day boundary, the pill updates to the
day just entered.

Covering the inline per-day separator is fine and expected - once the floating
pill updates correctly it shows the same date as the separator it overlaps, so
there's no visible conflict. The current bug is only that the pill is frozen at
the first loaded date, so it covers separators with a stale/wrong date.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a chat with multiple days of history (directly or via a date jump).
2. Note the floating date pill shows the first loaded day.
3. Scroll across several day boundaries in either dir

issues.title: [Bug]: Media files whose Telegram `file_name` contains newline (`\n`) or carriage-return (`\r`) characters can cause media downloads to fail on Windows.
issues.body:
### Version

7.33.4

### Deployment Method

Manual/Python

### Database Type

SQLite (default)

### Bug Description

## Problem

Media files whose Telegram `file_name` contains newline (`\n`) or carriage-return (`\r`) characters can cause media downloads to fail on Windows.

For example, this filename:

`Werner Furrer\nKlima-Wandel?\rKlima-Schwindel!.pdf`

was previously passed through `sanitize_media_filename()` unchanged.

This resulted in a download path such as:

`..._shared\5276091715084619737_Werner Furrer\nKlima-Wandel?\rKlima-Schwindel!.pdf.146104.1883193060688.part`

and Windows raised:

`OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument`

The media download was retried five times and ultimately failed.

## Cause

`sanitize_media_filename()` currently removes path separators and NUL characters, but does not remove other Windows-invalid control characters such as `\n` and `\r`.

## Proposed fix

Sanitize control characters in the filename before returning it.

For example, change `sanitize_media_filename()` in `src/message_utils.py` to:

```python
def sanitize_media_filename(name: str) -> str:
    """Strip path components and invalid control characters from a media filename."""
    name = name.replace("\\", "/")
    name = os.path.basename(name)
    name = name.replace("\x00", "")

    # Windows does not allow control characters (0x00–0x1F) in filenames.
    name = "".join("_" if ord(ch) < 32 else ch for ch in name)

    if name in ("", ".", ".."):
        return "_"

    return name
```

I tested the fix with:

```text
IN : 'Werner Furrer\nKlima-Wandel?\rKlima-Schwindel!.pdf'
OUT: 'Werner Furrer_Klima-Wandel__Klima-Schwindel!.pdf'
```

After applying the change, the previously failing pending media downloads completed successfully:

`Pending media retry: 5 downloaded, 0 ski

issues.title: [Bug]: Audio auto-advance stops partway through large chats — runaway guard trips on consecutive page-loads instead of no-progress
issues.body:
### Version

7.32.0

### Deployment Method

Docker Compose

### Database Type

PostgreSQL

### Bug Description

7.32.0's chronological audio queue works, but auto-advance halts partway through
a large chat. In a chat with 1,764 voice notes, pressing "next" repeatedly
advances correctly, then stops moving forward after roughly 40 tracks with
hundreds of notes still ahead. Manually clicking the next voice message resumes
playback and re-arms auto-advance, so the queue data is intact - it just stops
paging.

Network trace: the queue pages backward through the media endpoint and then
simply stops after 9 requests, with no "ended" event and no error in the console:

  media?types=voice&limit=50&before_id=..._3739_voice
  ..._3653 -> _3350 -> _3150 -> _2982 -> _2754 -> _2647 -> _2572 -> _2428
  (stops; no further before_id requests)

This looks like the "cap consecutive auto-page-loads so a queue can never run
away" guard described in #254. The guard is worth having, but the trip condition
is wrong: it counts consecutive page-loads, and a legitimate deep queue (a chat
with thousands of voice notes) is indistinguishable from a runaway by that
measure. So healthy large chats hit the cap and stop.

The condition it should trip on is page-loads WITHOUT playback progress. A real
listener advances a track between loads; a runaway loads pages while playback
goes nowhere. Suggested fix: reset the consecutive-load counter whenever a track
actually plays (or reaches "ended"), so the guard only fires on the true runaway
case - many loads with zero tracks played - and a genuine listener can page to
the end of a chat of any size (I'd want a 1,764-note chat, or a hypothetical
300k-note one, to play through completely).

### Expected Behavior

Auto-advance should continue paging and playing

issues.title: Listener: recover edits and deletions missed during downtime from Telegram's update state
issues.body:
When the listener is down (a restart, a crash, a network outage), every edit, deletion and reaction made in that time is lost to it. Today the only way to recover them is `SYNC_DELETIONS_EDITS`, which re-reads stored messages by id at Telegram's limit of about 300 per 30 s. On large archives that takes days (#608).

Telegram's own apps solve this differently. They keep their position in the update stream (pts) and, after reconnecting, ask Telegram for what they missed with `updates.getDifference` and `updates.getChannelDifference`. That returns the missed deletions and edits directly.

Telethon already writes that position to the session's `update_state` table every 60 s and on disconnect, but only reads it back when the client is built with `catch_up=True`. The archive never sets it (`telegram_archive/config.py`), so a restart starts from a fresh state.

What needs working out before we turn it on:

- Replayed deletions arrive as one burst and would trip the mass-deletion limiter (10 per 30 s).
- After a long outage Telegram answers `channelDifferenceTooLong` for busy channels, and Telethon drops that silently. Those chats need a fallback, such as a windowed re-check (`SYNC_DELETIONS_EDITS_DAYS`).
- A crash can move the saved position past an update that was never stored.
- `docs/configuration/listener.md` says a restart keeps no update state. That's right about behaviour, but wrong about the disk.

Refs #608

issues.title: [Feature]: Indicate which days have messages in the Jump to Date calendar
issues.body:
### Feature Category

Web Viewer

### Problem Statement

The Jump to Date calendar renders every day identically, with no signal of
which dates actually contain messages. Picking a date is blind guessing, and
after landing on an empty day there is no way to tell from the calendar that
the emptiness was expected. The native client's calendar shows at a glance
which days have content.

### Proposed Solution

Visually distinguish days with messages from days without: gray out / disable
empty days, and mark non-empty days (bold, a dot, or subtle background). No
media previews needed - a binary has-messages signal is enough.

Data cost is one cheap query per displayed month:
  SELECT (date AT TIME ZONE :tz)::date AS day, count(*)
  FROM messages WHERE chat_id = :chat AND date BETWEEN :month_start AND :month_end
  GROUP BY 1;
served by a small endpoint like
  /api/chats/{chat_id}/messages/dates?month=2026-07&timezone=...
and fetched when the calendar opens or the month changes.

Optional niceties, not required: a count-based intensity (heatmap), and a
tooltip with the day's message count. Disabling empty days would also remove
the confusing empty-jump case entirely.

### Alternatives Considered

- Media previews per day like the native client: much heavier (thumbnail
  selection and serving) for little navigation benefit over a binary marker.
- Clamping empty jumps to the nearest non-empty day server-side: helps, but
  the user still can't see where messages are before clicking.

### Additional Context

Running 7.28.0, PostgreSQL. Independent of the date-jump scroll bug
- but both affect the same navigation flow, so fixing
them together would make calendar navigation fully trustworthy.

### Contribution

- [ ] I would be willing to help implement this feature

issues.title: [Bug]: Historical backfill drops service-action metadata that the live listener preserves
issues.body:
### What happens

`_process_message` (src/telegram_backup.py) stores service messages during historical backfills but discards `message.action` entirely: `raw_data` is enriched for albums, forwards, post authors and polls, while service actions are dropped.

The live listener has preserved this metadata since v6.0.0 (`raw_data.service_type` / `action_type` / `new_title`, src/listener.py). The two ingestion paths are inconsistent: an event captured live keeps its payload; the same event reached through a backfill loses it, and the loss is permanent.

### Why it matters

Forum topic history is the visible casualty. `forum_topics.title` is overwritten on rename (upsert in src/db/adapter.py), and the `MessageActionTopicCreate` / `MessageActionTopicEdit` service messages are stored with no action payload. After a backfill there is no way to audit when a topic was created or renamed, or what it was called before.

### Reproduction (synthetic forum)

1. In a test forum supergroup: create a topic, post in it, rename it.
2. Run a historical backup of that chat.
3. Inspect the DB: the service rows exist (empty text) but raw_data carries no action info; the previous topic title is gone.

### Proposed fix (minimal, no schema change)

Mirror the listener convention in `_process_message`:

- `raw_data.service_type = "service"`;
- `raw_data.action_type` = normalized action class name (`topic_create`, `topic_edit`, `chat_edit_title`, ...);
- `raw_data.new_title` via the existing `_text_with_entities_to_string` helper, only when the action carries a title.

Topic history becomes reconstructible with existing columns: `topic_create` links via `messages.id == forum_topics.id`; `topic_edit` via `reply_to_top_id`. No migration (raw_data is already JSON), no new logs, no viewer changes.

issues.title: [Feature]: Option to limit SYNC_DELETIONS_EDITS to recent messages
issues.body:
### Feature Category

Backup Process

### Problem Statement

Thanks again for 9.5.0, it's running well on our research archive.

We've hit a scaling limit with SYNC_DELETIONS_EDITS. Each sweep re-checks every stored message, one get_messages call per 100 ids, and Telegram returns a FloodWait of 27 to 29 s after almost every call. Measured: 27,399 messages took about 45 minutes (about 36,000 per hour). We plan to archive 100 to 500 signal channels, about 1 to 5 million messages, so one sweep would take 1 to 6 days.

The listener catches deletions within a second in our tests, so the sweep is only our safety net for outages, and the deletions we care about mostly happen within days of posting.

Request: a setting to re-check only messages posted in the last N days, for example SYNC_DELETIONS_EDITS_DAYS=14 (0 = all, the current behaviour), ideally with its own schedule for an occasional full pass.

Two questions:
1. Is there already a way to do this that we missed?
2. Would a pass that reads recent history and treats missing ids as deleted hit fewer FloodWaits than get_messages by id?

Happy to test a pre-release.

### Proposed Solution

A setting such as SYNC_DELETIONS_EDITS_DAYS=14 so each sweep only re-checks messages posted in the last N days (0 = all, the current behaviour), plus an optional separate schedule for an occasional full re-check, for example weekly.

### Alternatives Considered

Running the sweep once a night instead of every 6 hours (still days long at 1 million messages), or turning SYNC_DELETIONS_EDITS off and relying on the listener alone (no safety net for outages).

### Additional Context

_No response_

### Contribution

- [ ] I would be willing to help implement this feature

issues.title: [Bug]: SQLite realtime push fails with "Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable"
issues.body:
### Version

v9.4.1

### Deployment Method

Docker Compose

### Database Type

SQLite (default)

### Bug Description

On SQLite, the backup's realtime push to the viewer fails, so open viewer tabs never update live. Capture is unaffected.

`RealtimeNotifier._notify_http` sends `json=payload`, which uses plain `json.dumps` and raises on the payload's `datetime` values ([realtime.py#L312-L351](https://github.com/GeiserX/Telegram-Archive/blob/v9.4.1/telegram_archive/realtime.py#L312-L351)). The PostgreSQL path passes `default=_json_serializer` (L305). After the first failure `_http_push_failed` logs at DEBUG, so the logs show the error only once.

Suggested fix: send `data=json.dumps(payload, default=_json_serializer)` with `Content-Type: application/json` (`content=` for httpx).

### Expected Behavior

Pushes reach `/internal/push` and open viewer tabs update live, as on PostgreSQL.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the stock compose with SQLite and `ENABLE_LISTENER=true`.
2. Receive a message in a tracked chat while a viewer tab is open.
3. The message appears only after a refresh, and the viewer logs no `POST /internal/push`.

### Logs

```shell
telegram_archive.realtime - WARNING - HTTP notification failed: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable (later failures are logged at DEBUG until a push succeeds)
```

### Environment

`drumsergio/telegram-archive` and `drumsergio/telegram-archive-viewer` 9.4.1, linux/amd64.

issues.title: Single-file downloads are sequential (gotd Stream), capped at ~1.3 MB/s even with Premium
issues.body:
**Version:** v3.0.10 (image `ghcr.io/botnick/telegram-media-downloader:latest`, revision `b22a0688`), Docker on Linux.

**What happens**

A single large file downloads at a flat ~1.3 MB/s. I measured 1.29 MB/s over 7.5 minutes on a 1.59 GB video (61 MB to 640 MB). The account has Telegram Premium, `download.maxSpeed` is `0` and `download.concurrent` is `10`. The rate stays the same over the whole file, so it does not look like a Telegram tier limit.

**Likely cause**

`core-service/internal/telegram/attachment.go`, `downloadMedia`:

```go
pool, err = client.DC(ctx, a.DC, 1)   // or client.Pool(1)
...
_, err = downloader.NewDownloader().Download(tg.NewClient(pool), a.Location).WithVerify(true).Stream(ctx, w)
```

gotd documents `Builder.Stream` as sequential ("NB: in this mode download can't be parallel", `telegram/downloader/builder.go` in gotd v0.115.0). Each file is fetched as one 512 KB part per round trip over one connection. At 1.29 MB/s that is about 2.5 parts per second, so the speed is set by per-request latency, not bandwidth. `download.concurrent` only helps when several different files download at the same time.

**Suggestion**

Use `Builder.Parallel` with `WithThreads(n)` on an `io.WriterAt` (the `.part` file), with a pool larger than 1 connection to the media DC. A setting for threads per file (for example `download.threadsPerFile`) would let users tune this. gotd v0.115.0 already provides `WithThreads` and `Parallel`.

**Not yet checked**

I have not compared against Telegram Desktop for the same file on the same network.

issues.title: Docker build references missing pre-download-models.js
issues.body:
## Summary

The repository references `scripts/pre-download-models.js`, but the file is missing.

## Evidence

- `package.json` defines `npm run pre-download-models` as `node scripts/pre-download-models.js`.
- `Dockerfile` runs `node scripts/pre-download-models.js || true` during the runtime image build.
- The build emits:

```text
Error: Cannot find module '/app/scripts/pre-download-models.js'
```

## Impact

The Docker build succeeds only because the command is masked by `|| true`, but the intended model pre-warming never happens. The first NSFW scan downloads the model at runtime, increasing cold-start latency and breaking the expected prewarm behavior for offline or restricted deployments. `npm run pre-download-models` also fails directly.

## Reproduction

```bash
npm run pre-download-models
# or
 docker build -t telegram-media-downloader .
```

## Expected behavior

Either restore/implement `scripts/pre-download-models.js` so it preloads the configured default model, or remove the stale package script and Dockerfile step and document that model downloads are intentionally lazy.

- A whole forum in one pass. Messages are sorted into topics as they arrive.
- The chat is split into message-id ranges that several workers download at once. Telegram limits each account separately, so every extra account adds about as much speed as the first.
- Progress is committed to SQLite every 100 messages. An interrupted run resumes where it stopped, and later runs fetch only new messages and append them to the files, so a repeat run of a large chat takes seconds. When a forum topic is renamed, its folder is renamed too.
- Everything the Telegram app shows with a message, not only its text: rich messages laid out in blocks, file names and sizes, link previews, polls and checklists, places and contacts, buttons with their links, quotes in replies, replies to other chats, forward sources, author signatures and admin titles, fact checks, service actions with their details.
- Optional extras, each a toggle: reactions and views, formatting with hidden links, comments under channel posts, and Telegram's export mode (see [Extras](#extras)).
- Filters by date range, author or message type, such as links or documents.

## Quick start

1. Create an app at [my.telegram.org](https://my.telegram.org) → *API development tools* and note its `api_id` and `api_hash`.
2. Install and run:

Number, [p] search public chats, or type to search again > 1

Search chat (name, @username, id or t.me link; Enter: your dumps, /: settings): forum
   1) Forum Club  @forumclub  [forum]  2/2 accounts
   2) Forum News  @forumnews  [channel]  1/2 accounts
Number, [p] search public chats, or type to search again > 1

Forum Club  [forum]  id -1001234567890

- Answering `f` instead of `Y` asks for filters for this one dump.
- When a dump is done, `o` opens it in the browser (with the `html` extra) and `f` opens the folder.
- **Ctrl+C** stops the dump; the next run resumes it.
- If Telegram is blocked in your network, set `TG_PROXY` in `.env`, for example `TG_PROXY=socks5://127.0.0.1:1080`.
- The interactive mode is colored in a terminal; set `NO_COLOR=1` to turn colors off.

```

A filtered dump gets its own database and folder, for example `out/1234567890_My_Chat_since-2026-01-01_links/`, so it never mixes with the full dump. Filters can be combined. They work with whole-chat dumps, not with `--topics`.

When the whole chat is already dumped, date and author filters are applied to the saved copy: the whole chat is brought up to date first, then the filtered folder is written from it without downloading the messages again. `--type` always asks Telegram, since the saved copy does not know which messages hold links.

### Performance

Measured on a large forum supergroup (several hundred thousand messages):

| Accounts | Speed | Full dump |
|---|---|---|

## Output

With the `html` extra the chat folder gets **`index.html`**: double-click it to read the dump in a browser, with no network and no server. Topics are in a sidebar; the chat opens at the newest messages, replies jump to the quoted message, and there is search (`/`, Enter for the next match), a jump to a date or a message id, and links like `index.html#topic/12/msg/1042`. Its data lies in the hidden `.reader/` folder next to it, in parts of 10,000 messages; a repeat run rewrites only the newest part of each topic that got new messages, so it takes a fraction of a second. Times are shown in your local timezone, while the text files keep UTC.

Each topic folder contains:

| `id` | message id |
| `date`, `edit_date` | ISO 8601, UTC |
| `topic_id` | forum topic (`1` = General, `null` in non-forum chats) |
| `sender_id`, `sender` | author id and display name |
| `text` | message text |
| `reply_to`, `reply_top` | replied-to message and thread root |

| `media` | media type (`MessageMediaPhoto`, `MessageMediaDocument`, ...) |
| `action` | service message type (`MessageActionTopicCreate`, ...) |
| `grouped_id` | album id |
| `extra` | everything else the app shows, see below |
| `text_md`, `views`, `forwards`, `replies`, `reactions` | only with the matching [extras](#extras) |

issues.title: perf(export): 대량 내보내기 1단계 요청 대기(waitTime) 적응형 검토
issues.body:
## 배경

대량 대화방 내보내기의 **체감 시간을 지배하는 요인**은 메시지를 훑는 1단계의 요청 간 고정 대기다.

`src/features/export/lib/exportChat.ts` 의 `iterMessages`:

```ts
for await (const message of client.iterMessages(peer, {
  limit: undefined,
  reverse: true,
  waitTime: 1,   // 요청 하나 끝날 때마다 1초 강제 대기
  ...
}))
```

GramJS 는 메시지를 **요청당 100건씩** 받는다. `waitTime: 1` 은 그 요청 사이마다 무조건 1초를 쉰다.

- 100건 = 최소 1초
- 24만 건 ≈ 2,400 요청 = **순수 강제 대기만 약 40분** (실제 다운로드 시간 별개)

## 개선 여지

이 파일에는 이미 `invoke` 래퍼가 있어서 FLOOD_WAIT 이 걸리면 **정확히 그 초만큼 자고 재시도**한다(진행 화면에 남은 시간도 실어 보낸다). 즉 요청 제한 방어가 **이중**이라, 선제적 1초 대기가 과보수적일 수 있다.

무대기로 시작해서 FLOOD 를 실제로 맞을 때만 백오프하는 **적응형(auto)** 으로 바꾸면 대형 대화방이 크게 빨라질 여지가 있다. (같은 논리가 미디어 다운로드 동시성 `FILE_CONCURRENCY = 3` 에도 적용될 수 있다 — 사용자 옵션이 아니라 적응형으로.)

## 왜 지금 바로 안 하나 (위험)

"얼마나 자주 FLOOD 를 맞느냐" 는 대화방 크기·계정·시간대·서버 상태에 따라 달라서, **실측 없이 감으로 조이면 오히려 FLOOD 를 더 자주 맞아 느려질 수** 있다. FLOOD_WAIT 은 보통 수십~수백 초라 1초 아끼려다 300초를 맞으면 손해다.

앞서 처리한 개선(화면용 썸네일/캐시 스킵, 미디어 롤링 윈도우)은 출력 무변경·무위험이라 바로 반영했지만, 이건 성격이 다르다.

## 제안하는 순서

1. **계측 먼저 (안전, 로직 무변경).** 1단계가 끝날 때 콘솔에 총 요청 수 · 전체 소요 · 순수 대기 시간 · FLOOD 발생 횟수와 각 대기 초를 찍는다. `waitTime` 을 환경값 등으로 빼서 같은 대화방을 값만 바꿔 재측정하기 쉽게 한다.
2. **실측.** 큰 대화방으로 `waitTime` 1 → 0.5 → 0 을 돌려 무대기 시 FLOOD 빈도를 숫자로 확인.
3. **결정.** 측정값을 근거로 고정값을 낮출지 / 적응형으로 갈지 정한다. `FILE_CONCURRENCY` 도 같은 데이터로 함께 판단.

## 관련 코드

- `src/features/export/lib/exportChat.ts` — `iterMessages({ waitTime: 1 })`, `client.invoke` FLOOD 래퍼, `EXPORT_FLOOD_SLEEP_THRESHOLD`, `FILE_CONCURRENCY`

## 참고

- 사용자 노출 옵션으로 빼는 건 안 한다 — 안전 상한선이지 취향이 아니고, "아무것도 저장 안 함" 앱 정체성과 저장형 설정이 충돌한다. 적응형(auto)이 방향.

[English](README.en.md) | [简体中文](README.md)

TGArchiveManager 是一个本地 Windows 桌面工具，用于管理 Telegram 内容归档流程。
项目基于 Python 3.10+、PySide6、Telethon 和 SQLite 实现。

> 当前状态：`v0.2.0` 公开预览。项目仍在持续完善，建议先使用测试账号和小范围聊天验证工作流。

> 当前状态：`v0.2.0` 公开预览。项目仍在持续完善，建议先使用测试账号和小范围聊天验证工作流。

当前 MVP 已覆盖：Telegram 登录、聊天同步、公开搜索、搜索结果管理和转发、聊天记录转发、消息备份、媒体下载、本地搜索、数据导出、日志排查和 Windows 打包发布。

## 界面预览

已支持的工作流：

- 使用 API ID/API Hash、手机验证码和可选二步验证密码登录 Telegram。
- 同步当前账号可访问的聊天，读取 Telegram 官方聊天文件夹/分组，并编辑本地标签。
- 通过多个 Telegram Bot Provider 执行 Bot 公开搜索，或在独立“TG 频道搜索”页指定已加入频道/群聊执行 TG 原生消息搜索，并保存标准化结果；TG 频道搜索结果可展示媒体大小或 Telegraph 图片数量。
- 当 Bot/TG 搜索结果、Telegram 消息文本、Bot 按钮或链接预览中出现 `telegra.ph` 链接时，识别为 Telegraph 图片页面卡片，解析标题、发布时间、作者/来源、图片数量和 Telegram 跳转链接；下载时按页面标题创建目录，并可限制图片下载数量。

- 真实配置、Telegram session、SQLite 数据库、日志、下载、导出和本地构建产物均被排除在版本控制之外。
- 发布 Issue、PR、测试记录或截图前，请移除手机号、聊天内容、API Hash、验证码和密码。
- 软件只处理当前账号有权访问的内容，不提供大量加群、成员采集或越权访问能力。
- 安全问题请按 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) 私下报告。

- 设置

## Windows 打包

推荐重复打包命令：

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\build_windows.ps1
```

构建产物输出到：

- `data`

干净 Windows 环境验收步骤见：[release-checklist.md](docs/release-checklist.md)。

issues.title: Add an English README
issues.body:
## Goal
Add an English README so non-Chinese users can evaluate and run TGArchiveManager.

## Scope
- Keep the Chinese README as the primary document.
- Add `README.en.md`.
- Link both language versions near the top of each README.
- Keep installation, privacy, and compliance guidance aligned.

## Acceptance criteria
- English setup commands match the current Python 3.10+ workflow.
- No real credentials, sessions, local paths, or user data appear in examples.
- `python scripts\preflight_check.py --root .` still passes.

issues.title: Document and test a clean Windows installation
issues.body:
## Goal
Validate the setup instructions on a clean Windows 10/11 environment.

## Tasks
- Create a Python 3.10+ virtual environment.
- Install `requirements.txt`.
- Run `python main.py --check` and `python -m unittest discover -s tests`.
- Record any missing prerequisite or unclear README step.

## Privacy
Use the example configuration only. Do not attach real API credentials, Telegram sessions, logs, screenshots with account data, or local databases.
